summary: Frontend-only test of v1.7.0 AKA titles, film-only Cast Insights and the new Director Insights. Used the simulated electronAPI harness (auto_match_harness.init_script) and a mocked TMDB that includes alternative_titles, known_for_department and director profile_path. New file: /app/tests/test_iter40_aka_directors.py. Results: 41/41 checks pass and there were no page errors. (1) fetchMovieDetails PASS. The request includes append_to_response=credits,release_dates,external_ids,alternative_titles. aka = original_title, then US/GB/CA/AU/IE/NZ titles. Duplicates are removed case-insensitively ('the film' dropped), the main title and FR/DE titles are excluded, and the list is capped at 6 ([Le Film, The Film, A1, A2, A3, A4]). When there are no aliases, aka = []. directors = [{name, profile_path w185}] and cast entries have dept. (2) Card and detail PASS. Medium and large grids show 'aka <first>' with the tooltip 'Also known as: a · b · ...'. Small grid and cards with empty aka show no line. The detail window shows the movie-aka line, and it is hidden for aka []. Search matches AKA titles ('a3' and 'original 103'). (3) Background auto-fill PASS. Only matched non-TV films with aka undefined (or no metadata) are fetched: 101, 102, 103 and 105. Not fetched: 104 (aka []), tv500 and the unmatched card. After a reload there are no new fetches. With 205 cards, the first batch is exactly 200, max concurrency is 2, and the remaining 5 come in the next batch; all cards end with an aka list. (4) Cast Insights PASS. Excluded: 13 media_type 'tv' cards, 13 isSeries cards (S01E01 parts, no media_type), Music films (genre as a string and as {name}), Documentaries, 'Himself' credits and a dept 'Sound' credit. Legacy cast with no dept is still counted. The header reads (6 actors across 12 movies). (5) Director Insights PASS. The header reads (4 directors across 12 films). Most Films: Dir A 6, Dir D 4, Dir B 2, Dir C 2 (B and C are split from the legacy 'Dir B, Dir C' string). Top-rated shows only Dir A (6 films, ★ 6.7; Dir D has 4, below the minimum of 5). Genre range lists 4 directors. Pairs: 10 rows, Actor X-V with Dir A = 6. The 6th acting credit, Cameo and Singer are excluded. Dir A's photo is shown. The section is hidden when no films have directors. TV, Series, Concert and Doc directors are excluded. (6) Regressions PASS: iter39 run_fd_type_switch and run_fd_remove (the plurals are now correct: '1 title'), and iter38 run_loose_heuristics 6/6 and run_nested_badge.

issues: isFilmCard drops every film with the TMDB 'Music' genre. TMDB has no separate 'Musical' genre, so real acted films are removed from both cast and director insights: La La Land, Whiplash, Bohemian Rhapsody, A Star Is Born, Rocketman, Elvis, Walk the Line. The Himself/Herself and dept filters already remove concert musicians, so consider excluding Music only when it is combined with Documentary, or when most of the billed cast are Self credits.

Director Insights: when Top-Rated has only 1 row, the 4-column grid stretches that card to the height of the Pairs card (10 rows), which leaves a large empty card. Cosmetic only; consider items-start.

action_items: MEDIUM (product decision): reconsider excluding the whole 'Music' genre in peopleStats.isFilmCard, because it hides musicals and music biopics from Cast and Director Insights.
LOW: Director pairs slice(0,5) is applied after filtering out Self and non-acting credits, so the 6th or 7th billed actor can count as 'top-5 billed'. Fine if intended.
critical_code_review_comments: isActingCredit uses known_for_department, which describes the person, not the role. A real acting role by someone known mainly for Directing, Writing or Sound (for example a rapper or singer who acts) is excluded. This is acceptable per the request ('no musicians'), but note that it is a heuristic.

needsBg re-fetches cards with media_type undefined whose aka is undefined, including untagged multi-part series that isSeries() detects. fetchDetails then treats them as movies. Consider also skipping isSeries(m) in needsBg.
bgTriedRef is in memory only. Titles that fail (404 or network) are retried on every app launch. This is harmless but repeats requests.

The card aka line shows the original-language title first, which may be in a non-Latin script (for example Japanese). Consider preferring the first English alternative title on the card and keeping the original title in the tooltip and detail window.

success_rate.frontend: 100% of requested checks (41/41) plus regressions; 1 MEDIUM product/design concern (Music genre exclusion)

seed_data_creation: None. Isolated browser contexts with a sessionStorage/localStorage-mocked library only.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Usage: g={'page':page}; exec(open('/app/tests/test_iter40_aka_directors.py').read(), g); await g['run_aka_bg']() / run_insights() / run_no_directors() / run_batch(). Uses auto_match_harness.init_script (its EULA version matches package.json; auto_enrich_harness.init_script hardcodes eula 1.6.8, so it lands on the landing page in v1.7.0). AkaMock serves movie details with alternative_titles. Stats URL is URL+'stats' (hash router). Background enrich starts about 10s after load.
